premises: Let W = GF(2)^n for an arbitrary finite n >= 0.
Let U <= W be a subspace with dimension d.
Let V = (U_1,...,U_m) be an indexed subspace arrangement with m >= 2 distinct occurrence identities and U_i = U geometrically for every i.
A linear layout is a permutation of the m indexed occurrences; equal geometry does not identify occurrences.

At cut i, L_i is the span of occurrences in positions < i, R_i is the span of occurrences in positions >= i, boundary_i = L_i intersect R_i, and cut width is dim(boundary_i), matching the frozen B5.2B cut-certificate definition.
statement.conclusion: Every linear layout of V has maximum cut width exactly d; therefore the path-width of V is exactly d.
statement.internal_cut_clause: For every 1 <= i < m, both sides contain at least one indexed copy of U, so L_i = U, R_i = U, boundary_i = U and width_i = d.
statement.excluded_case: m = 1 is not covered; its only two cuts are endpoints, so its maximum cut width is 0 even when d > 0.
